analysis.title: Marketcolour (Ioannis Blekos, GS Sales & Trading) 6 Nov 2026
key_insights: US equities sold off sharply on 11/5: SPX -436bps to 7353, NDX -636bps to 26629, RTY -455bps to 2729. S&P 500 and Russell 2000 had their worst sessions since April 2025 and the Nasdaq its worst day since March 2020. All sectors fell, Tech -7.30%, Industrials -4.12%, Staples -0.67%.
VIX rose 70% to 28.15. The Nasdaq VIX had its biggest one-day move since Covid.
Nvidia (-9.26%) and Micron (-17.46%) accounted for 11.41% and 11.06% of the NDX move respectively.

GS AI Semis basket (GSCBSMHX) fell 12.16% and the Data Centers basket (GSTMTDAT) fell 12.03%. Semis have underperformed the market by more than 15 points over 5 days, the biggest bout of underperformance since 2002.
Supply in semis/AI continued, but the offsetting demand for hyperscalers/Mag 7 and defensive tech that supported the index the prior day did not return. Asset managers were net sellers.

GS desk flow: inbound call volume was a 10 out of 10 but overall activity a 5 out of 10, and high-touch activity was much quieter than Wednesday. Price action looked driven by top-down macro instruments, with ETFs about 32% of the tape. Hedge funds finished roughly balanced while actively trading their short books.

GS Prime data: global fundamental long/short hedge funds fell 1.3% (a -2 SD move), mostly from beta, and are +8.7% YTD. TMT funds fell more than 4% and are roughly flat YTD, down from about +24% before the June/July AI sell-off. Multi-strat funds fell 1.4% with momentum down 3.7 SD.

GS estimates October nonfarm payrolls at +75k vs consensus +65k and a three-month average of +51k, with average hourly earnings +0.3% m/m and unemployment unchanged at 4.2%, both in line with consensus.

GS lowered its end-2026 gold forecast to $4,150/toz and end-2027 to $4,800/toz (from $5,400), citing the Fed's hawkish shift for positioning, while keeping a constructive long-term view on central bank buying of 60 tonnes/month through 2026-27.
Airbnb said about 40% of customer support issues in Q3 2026 were resolved without a human agent, and support cost per booking fell more than 17% y/y.
GS cut Kuehne & Nagel to Neutral from Buy, expecting a cooling container market in FY27 and seeing less upside from margin mean reversion.

IAG Q3 2026 EBIT of €1.73bn was 5% below company consensus of €1.81bn, partly from disruption costs. Daimler Truck Q4 was 1% ahead but orders missed by 9%. Amadeus was in line with FCF better than consensus and guidance reiterated at the low end.

market_movers.rationale: Kuehne & Nagel (no US listing) cut to Neutral from Buy on expected FY27 container market cooling and less upside from margin mean reversion. GS EBIT is 3% above visible alpha consensus for Q4 and under 2% ahead for FY28.
Nvidia fell 9.26% on 11/5 and accounted for 11.41% of the NDX move amid continued semis/AI supply.
Micron fell 17.46% on 11/5 and accounted for 11.06% of the NDX move.

earnings_insights: Airbnb Q3 2026: about 40% of customer support issues resolved without a human agent, support cost per booking down more than 17% y/y.

IAG Q3 2026 (reported): EBIT €1.73bn vs company consensus €1.81bn, a 5% miss. Passenger revenue missed on volume/RPK, RASK +4% in line with consensus, non-fuel unit costs +3.4% y/y vs GS estimate of 2.7%.

Daimler Truck Q4 (reported): 1% ahead of expectations, helped by FX and tariff reimbursement. Orders missed by 9%. FY26 guidance maintained. Soft Q4 guidance implies North America about 11% vs consensus 11.8%, Mercedes-Benz above corridor (>8% vs consensus 8.4%), Buses 9-10% vs consensus 10.5%.

Amadeus Q3 (reported): revenue €1.74bn vs consensus €1.74bn, operating income €506.7mn vs consensus €521.7mn, FCF €564.2mn vs consensus €532.6mn, EBITDA €694.1mn vs consensus €694.4mn. Guidance reiterated at the low end.
Kuehne & Nagel: GS EBIT 3% above visible alpha consensus for Q4 and under 2% ahead for FY28.
